name: Shemaiah
title: The Prophet Who Warned Rehoboam
summary: Shemaiah was a man of God and a prophet who served during the reign of King Rehoboam in Judah. He is best known for warning Rehoboam against going to war with the northern tribes after the kingdom split, and for explaining that Shishak's invasion from Egypt was God's judgment on Judah's unfaithfulness.

keyEvents.title: Warned Rehoboam Against Civil War
keyEvents.description: After the ten northern tribes broke away from Rehoboam, Shemaiah spoke God's word to the king and all Judah and Benjamin, forbidding them to go to war against their brothers in Israel. The people obeyed the Lord's word and returned home.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as a Source in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Shemaiah's deeds and prophetic words are cited as one of the sources for Rehoboam's history, highlighting his significance as a historical and prophetic authority.

keyEvents.title: Delivered God's Message to Rehoboam Regarding the Civil War
keyEvents.description: In the parallel account in Chronicles, Shemaiah conveyed God's word to Rehoboam and all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, telling them not to fight against their brothers, for the division of the kingdom was from the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Explained Shishak's Invasion as God's Judgment
keyEvents.description: When Pharaoh Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem, Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah and said that the Lord had abandoned them because they had abandoned him. The leaders humbled themselves, and the Lord relented from his judgment.
